To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the calcitonins in cancer are not the same as those of hypercalcemia or medullary carcinoma.
1) the immunoreactivity of the calcitonin of MCT is heterogeneous; 2) the immunoreactive material in serum from patients with cancer of lung and breast is heterogeneous;

there is a family of calcitonins in man which includes a form which is produced by normal subjects in response to hypercalcemia, another form produced by medullary carcinoma thyroid (MCT) and two others produced by cancer of breast and lung.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the heterogeneity of human calcitonins and its clinical significance.
the development of a new approach for the diagnosis and treatment of cancer of the lung, breast, and thyroid.

the heterogeneity of calcitonins of cancer and normal subjects and the use of antisera which recognize different molecular species of calcitonins in the diagnosis and follow-up of patients with cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the calcitonin of MCT is a unique and distinct molecule which is not found in other cancers.
the calcitonin in MCT is the same as that in normal thyroid and in the hypercalcemia of malignancy.
calcitonin levels are not diagnostic of MCT, but may be helpful in following patients with MCT.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immunoheterogeneity of calcitonin in man is not only a matter of molecular species, but also of epitopic determinants.
the calcitonins in the various cancers are immunoheterogeneous, but that the heterogeneity may be more related to the cancer than to the species of antiserum used.
the iCT of MCT is a heterogeneous group of molecules with a range of immunoreactivities and that a variety of antisera are required to detect all the immunologically distinct species of iCT.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a single assay for calcitonin is inadequate for diagnostic purposes.
there is no single assay for the detection of iCT in human serum.
there are different types of calcitonin in the body and that they are produced by different tissues.
